chapters.title: Chapter 1: Freedom of Information Act Framework
chapters.description: Introduces FOIA’s purpose, structure, and core mechanics that govern federal agency disclosure obligations and exemptions.
subtopics: Purpose and history of FOIA
Definitions: agency, records, requesters
Statutory duties to search and disclose
Nine exemptions and three exclusions: overview
Jurisdiction and remedies under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(B)
Constructive exhaustion and administrative timelines
Burden of proof on the government

chapters.title: Chapter 2: FOIA Litigation and Summary Judgment Practice
chapters.description: Explains how FOIA disputes are resolved in court, the role of agency declarations, and evidentiary tools used to adjudicate exemptions.
subtopics: Summary judgment as the primary vehicle in FOIA cases
Agency declarations and the presumption of good faith
Vaughn indices and categorical justifications
In camera review authority under § 552(a)(4)(B)
Record scope and supplementation
Appellate standards: de novo legal review with deference to expertise where appropriate

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Landmark Precedents on Exemption 7(A) and Ongoing Proceedings
chapters.description: Surveys foundational case law defining Exemption 7(A)’s protection for law-enforcement records where disclosure could interfere with pending or reasonably anticipated proceedings.
subtopics: NLRB v. Robbins Tire & Rubber Co.: categorical withholding to protect enforcement integrity
Citizens for Responsibility & Ethics in Washington v. DOJ (CREW): ‘pending or reasonably anticipated’ requirement; sufficiency and specificity of agency attestations
Silvia Patricia Miranda Juarez v. DOJ (DEA): continuing investigations and jeopardy from premature disclosure; whole-document withholding when intertwined
Center for National Security Studies v. DOJ (CNSS): accepted ‘tip-off’ interference rationale and deference in national security contexts

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Threshold for Exemption 7 – ‘Compiled for Law Enforcement Purposes’
chapters.description: Details the prerequisite showing that records were compiled for law enforcement purposes, including the rational nexus test and agency deference.
subtopics: Statutory text and structure of Exemption 7
Pratt v. Webster: the ‘rational nexus’ test
Campbell v. DOJ: applying Pratt and recognizing deference to the FBI
Per se law-enforcement agencies vs. mixed-function agencies
Connections to security risks or violations of federal law

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Exemption 7(A) Harms and Proof
chapters.description: Explains how agencies demonstrate interference with enforcement proceedings and how courts assess those claims.
subtopics: Recognized harms: tip-off, chilling witnesses, revealing scope and strategy
What counts as ‘proceedings’: criminal investigations and prospective cases
Acceptable specificity in declarations vs. impermissible vagueness
Use of categorical groupings for 7(A) and the limits on category breadth
Temporal considerations: staleness, updating declarations, and ongoing status confirmations

chapters.title: Chapter 6: National Security Deference in FOIA
chapters.description: Covers why and how courts afford deference to executive branch national security judgments within FOIA disputes.
subtopics: Doctrinal basis for deference in national security matters
CNSS and related D.C. Circuit authority
The mosaic theory and risk aggregation concepts
Balancing de novo review with institutional competence and secrecy needs
Interaction with law-enforcement exemptions, especially 7(A)

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Segregability Requirements and Meaningful Disclosure
chapters.description: Explores FOIA’s mandate to release reasonably segregable, meaningful, nonexempt information and the showing agencies must make.
subtopics: Statutory duty: § 552(b) and § 552(a)(8)(A)(ii)
Mead Data Central v. Air Force: ‘meaningful’ information vs. isolated words; interspersed content
Perioperative Services & Logistics v. VA: practical application and use of ex parte materials in segregability
Agency affidavits on non-segregability and court verification
When entire documents may be withheld as inextricably intertwined

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Categorical Withholdings, Vaughn Indices, and Adequate Descriptions
chapters.description: Details methods for justifying withholdings without revealing sensitive content, and the standards for category definitions.
subtopics: Purpose and structure of Vaughn submissions
Gallant v. NLRB: ‘sufficiently distinct’ categories standard
CREW guidance on category breadth and specificity
Pitfalls: overbroad categories and conclusory statements
Court tools for testing adequacy: sampling, in camera review

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Ex Parte and In Camera Submissions in FOIA
chapters.description: Explains when courts may rely on sealed and ex parte declarations, and how that practice fits within adversarial process and FOIA’s disclosure goals.
subtopics: Statutory basis under § 552(a)(4)(B)
Perioperative Services & Logistics v. VA: acceptance and limits of ex parte practice
Due process concerns and mitigating measures
Appellate review of sealed records and maintaining confidentiality
Party conduct: consent, failure to object, and consequences

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Appellate Review, Preservation, and Forfeiture in FOIA Cases
chapters.description: Covers how FOIA issues are reviewed on appeal and the consequences of not preserving arguments.
subtopics: De novo review of summary judgment rulings
Standards for reviewing agency affidavits and factual showings
Issue preservation in district court
Waiver vs. forfeiture on appeal (e.g., Khine v. DHS)
Remedies and dispositions: affirm, vacate, remand

chapters.title: Chapter 11: FOIA Improvement Act of 2016 and Modern Disclosure Standards
chapters.description: Outlines statutory updates that shape contemporary FOIA litigation, including segregability and foreseeable harm.
subtopics: The ‘foreseeable harm’ standard under § 552(a)(8)(A)(i) (overview)
Codified ‘reasonable steps’ to segregate under § 552(a)(8)(A)(ii)
Agency best practices for compliance post-2016
Interplay with Exemption 7(A) and national security assertions

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Evidentiary Burdens, Deference, and Context in FOIA
chapters.description: Synthesizes how burdens of production and persuasion operate alongside deference to law-enforcement expertise in FOIA disputes.
subtopics: Government’s burden to justify withholdings
Requester strategies to rebut with evidence of bad faith or insufficiency
Deference to specialized agencies like the FBI (Campbell; Clemente v. FBI)
Role of contextual evidence and public records in evaluating declarations
Judicial gatekeeping to prevent disclosure of sensitive enforcement details
